mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the sine rule for angle $x^\circ$
Applying inverse sine and solving for $x$

subparts.solution: By the sine rule: $\frac{\sin x^\circ}{8} = \frac{\sin 65^\circ}{10} \implies \sin x^\circ = \frac{8\sin 65^\circ}{10} \implies x = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{8\sin 65^\circ}{10}\right) \approx 46.5$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The sine rule in angle form is $\frac{\sin A}{a} = \frac{\sin B}{b}$.
step_by_step: Identify opposite pairs: $x^\circ$ opposite $8$, and $65^\circ$ opposite $10$.
Calculate using the inverse sine function.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Inverting the ratio by dividing angle by side instead of sine of angle by side.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the sine rule for angle $x^\circ$

subparts.solution: By the sine rule: $\frac{\sin x^\circ}{20} = \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{25} \implies \sin x^\circ = \frac{20\sin 35^\circ}{25} \implies x = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{20\sin 35^\circ}{25}\right) \approx 27.3$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use $\frac{\sin A}{a} = \frac{\sin B}{b}$ to solve for an unknown angle.
step_by_step: Match side $20$ with angle $x^\circ$ and side $25$ with angle $35^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calculator in radian mode instead of degree mode.
